name: Coral Reefs
genZNote: Coral reefs cover less than 1% of the ocean floor but support about a quarter of all known marine species — the most disproportionately important real estate on Earth.

sections.heading: 🪸 What Coral Reefs Are
bullets: Built by colonies of tiny animals called coral polyps, which secrete calcium carbonate skeletons that accumulate into reef structures over long timescales.

Most reef-building corals live in a mutually beneficial partnership with microscopic algae (zooxanthellae) living in their tissue, which provide the coral with food through photosynthesis and give reefs their vivid colour.
Reefs form mainly in warm, shallow, clear, nutrient-poor tropical waters, which is why they're concentrated in a band around the equator.

sections.heading: 🌍 Major Reef Regions
bullets: The Coral Triangle (Indonesia, Philippines, Papua New Guinea, Malaysia, Timor-Leste, Solomon Islands) is the world's richest reef biodiversity zone.
Australia's Great Barrier Reef is the largest single reef system on Earth.
The Red Sea's reefs (Egypt, Sudan, Saudi Arabia) are notably resilient to warm water.
India's reef systems include Lakshadweep, the Gulf of Mannar, and parts of the Andaman & Nicobar Islands.
The Mesoamerican Reef (Mexico, Belize, Guatemala, Honduras) is the world's second-largest barrier reef system.

sections.heading: ⚠️ Threats
bullets: Coral bleaching: when stressed by unusually warm water, corals expel their algae partners and turn white, and can die if warm conditions persist.
Ocean acidification (from the ocean absorbing excess atmospheric CO2) makes it harder for corals to build their calcium carbonate skeletons.
Physical damage from destructive fishing, coastal development, and unsustainable tourism.
Because reefs grow so slowly, recovery from severe bleaching or damage can take decades.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Coral reefs are structures built by colonial polyps in partnership with algae, forming the ocean's most biodiverse ecosystems despite covering under 1% of the seafloor.
keyFacts: Built by coral polyps + symbiotic algae (zooxanthellae).
Support roughly a quarter of all known marine species.
Coral Triangle = richest reef biodiversity zone.
Coral bleaching = stress response to warm water, algae expelled.
commonConfusion: Bleached coral isn't automatically dead — it can recover if favorable conditions return quickly enough.

highYieldFacts: Coral reefs: <1% of seafloor, ~25% of marine species.
Zooxanthellae = symbiotic algae giving coral its food and colour.
Coral Triangle and Great Barrier Reef are the two most cited major reef regions.
commonTraps: Bleaching ≠ death — it's a stress response; prolonged stress is what causes coral death.
mustRemember: Coral reefs = tiny footprint, massive biodiversity; threatened by warming and acidification.
